children: Singapore's three big banks have put between 3% and 5% of their loan books into data centres, roughly double the share at Japan's two largest lenders, research house CreditSights estimates.

In a report dated November 16, the Fitch Solutions-owned firm counted $20.7bn of direct data-centre financing at Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), or 1.8% of its credit exposure, and $16.3bn, or 1.9%, at Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (SMFG). American lenders typically hold about 2% of loans or less in the sector.

Those are modest numbers, and the banks lean on them. The sharper danger from a cooling AI cycle lies in the fee business lenders have built around arranging data-centre debt and selling most of it on. A slowdown would dent fee growth before it produced credit losses, according to CreditSights, and an underwriting commitment turns into balance-sheet risk the moment investors stop taking the paper as fast as planned. The borrowers are meanwhile spending faster than they earn.
Data-centre financing as a share of credit exposure (Japan) or total loans (US, Singapore). Source: CreditSights report of November 16, 2026; OCBC. IntelliNews
Tokyo sells it on

MUFG's own interim investor presentation puts its data-centre exposure at $20.8bn at the end of August, about JPY3.3 trillion at today's rate. Of that, 57% sits in the Americas, 19% in Asia, 14% in Japan and 10% in Europe. The bank passed on roughly 70% of its share of the data-centre project-finance deals it arranged between April and August to other investors, and about 90% on gigawatt-scale transactions.

SMFG is pulling back harder. 'This year we have adopted stricter standards on extending credit for data centre financing, for instance restricting ourselves to just hyperscalers with high credit standing,' chief executive Toru Nakashima told a press briefing on November 13,
Reuters
reported. He warned that a slowdown in data-centre investment could weigh on the group's results over the next six months.

The group's results presentation shows JPY2.1 trillion ($13.1bn) of data-centre project finance inside total exposure of JPY177 trillion. Hyperscalers are the off-takers on 80% of it, and SMFG sold down about 90% of the US data-centre project finance it originated in the year to September, against about 70% a year earlier. Mizuho Financial Group chief executive Masahiro Kihara named tougher curbs on US data-centre construction after the Democrats' midterm gains as a tail risk.
MUFG data-centre exposure by region at end-August 2026, % of $20.8bn. Source: Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group interim investor presentation. IntelliNews
Singapore lends next door

Singapore's lenders sit closer to the region's construction boom. DBS, OCBC and UOB were among seven banks behind DayOne's MYR15bn ($3.6bn) Johor package in October, and the three jointly arranged a SGD5bn ($3.9bn) loan backing KKR and Singtel's purchase of ST Telemedia Global Data Centres. The same trio was picked to run the Singapore-dollar tranche of Alphabet's planned debut Asian bond sale in November, the kind of fee income CreditSights expects the AI build-out to keep generating.
OCBC chief executive Tan Teck Long put data-centre lending at below 3% of a SGD372bn ($288bn) loan book at third-quarter results, with AI-related exposure under 1%,
The Asian Banker
reported. He prefers projects backed by established hyperscalers, with power supply and customers signed before any money is lent.
Spending ahead of the cash

Tencent shows how quickly the borrowers' arithmetic can shift. The Shenzhen-based group booked capital expenditures of CNY81.4bn ($12.2bn) in the third quarter, up from CNY52.8bn in the second and CNY13.0bn a year earlier, according to its results release. Free cash flow came to minus CNY69.1bn ($10.4bn), negative for a second quarter running, and net cash of CNY102.4bn a year ago has become net debt of CNY13.7bn.

Tencent attributes most of the outflow to prepayments for computing capacity, without which free cash flow would have been a positive CNY16.9bn. Cash actually paid out for capital expenditures was CNY65.1bn, its results presentation shows.
Tencent capital expenditures and free cash flow by quarter, CNY bn. Source: Tencent Holdings results releases and presentations. IntelliNews

Exposure that never shows up as a data-centre loan is harder to count. CreditSights singles out lending to private credit funds and technology companies as the hardest channel to measure, and expects regulators to scrutinise AI-related financing more closely as it grows. SMFG alone reports JPY10.5 trillion ($65.6bn) of financing to funds, though it says the borrowers are mostly investment grade and none of the loans has soured.

Big tech's build-out is increasingly paid for with borrowed money, from Tencent's swing into net debt to Alphabet's Singapore-dollar bonds, and arranging that debt feeds the banks' fee lines. Should investors balk, perhaps over the leadership turmoil at Nvidia, the first casualty would be the pipeline of deals that pays for Asian banks' investment-banking teams. A slower pipeline would leave more of the debt sitting on their balance sheets.
At that point Singapore's 3-5% looks a good deal less comfortable than Tokyo's 2%.

title: Singapore's banks carry more AI data-centre risk than Japan's megabanks
